# Recreation Prompt

Recreate **Darkwing Rizz Squadron**, a portrait-first browser arcade game. Preserve the mechanics of an aim-and-fire bubble shooter: the player controls a bottom-center launcher with pointer/touch aim, fires one projectile at a time, bounces shots off side walls, snaps projectiles into a staggered grid, clears connected same-color clusters of 3+, grants floating-cluster bonuses, updates score, and ends the run when the grid reaches the lower danger threshold.

Transform the presentation into a satirical Batman-inspired space shooter without using protected names: the player is a neon bat-wing cruiser, projectiles are rizz orbs, grid targets are rogue cape-drones, score is Clout, and failure is being Sector Clowned at the Cringe Line. Use neon noir cyan/magenta/gold palette, procedural Canvas silhouettes, animated Gotham Orbit background, compact esports HUD, meme-tone feedback, and one-thumb mobile readability.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Current implemented game identity
- genre: portrait bubble-shooter / aim-and-fire arcade game with space-shooter framing.
- objective: aim a launcher from the bottom, fire colored projectiles upward, attach them to a staggered grid, and clear same-color clusters of 3 or more for score.
- input model: pointer or touch aims the bottom launcher; click/tap on the canvas fires one projectile if no projectile is active; UI buttons use native click/tap.
- core loop: start mission, initialize five filled rows, aim, fire, wall-bounce projectile, snap to grid on collision/ceiling, resolve cluster and floating removals, update score, repeat until danger threshold is reached.
- fail/friction state: if non-matching placements let active bubbles descend/occupy rows near the bottom danger line, the run ends and a restart modal appears.

## Protected mechanics
- One-thumb pointer/touch aiming and tap-to-shoot from the bottom center.
- Single active projectile at a time with speed 15 and horizontal wall bounce.
- Staggered hex-like grid coordinates, neighbor lookup, snap placement, cluster detection, and floating-cluster bonus logic.
- Score semantics: cluster bubbles worth 10 each; floating bubbles worth 20 each.
- Start/restart/game-over state flow, HUD score visibility, and danger-line failure semantics.

## Remixed target
Darkwing Rizz Squadron reframes the protected bubble-shooter as a satirical neon-noir space shooter: a bat-eared cape-cruiser launches rizz orbs into rogue cape-drone clusters above Gotham Orbit. The presentation, HUD language, focal silhouette, procedural background, and feedback become competitive futuristic arcade energy while the mechanics remain unchanged.
